cultivar: Mainly small-leaf population tea, plus some early cultivars
processing: A green tea made from a single bud or one bud with one or two leaves, finished either flat or curled. It follows China's national green tea standard.
harvest_season: Early cultivars start after about 20 March and small-leaf population tea after about 1 April. Gardens get around seven pickings a year and close in early September; as with other Chinese greens, the first spring pickings are the most valued.
appearance_dry: Either flat, straight and smooth in emerald or yellow-green, or curled.
appearance_wet: Whole buds and young leaves, substantial in the hand.
taste_profile: High in aroma with dense, substantial buds that hold up over several steeps; a specific taste note beyond that is seldom recorded.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a sturdy green rather than a local rule: water just below boiling suits the dense buds, with a little less heat for the flat style.

vintage_note: Sold as a current-year green tea, with the spring pickings from late March and April the ones to look for, and best within about a year. Later rounds run through to September and are cheaper, so a date on the pack is worth checking.
description:
Longnan Green Tea is the regional appellation for tea from southeastern Gansu, one of the most northerly tea areas in China. That latitude is the reason to try it. Gansu is not a province most people link with tea at all, but this corner slopes toward Sichuan and Shaanxi and has a much milder, wetter climate.

The protected zone is a triangle where three counties meet: Wenxian, Wudu and Kangxian, 13 townships and 148 villages in all, with tea growing on acidic mountain soils below 1400 metres. Wide swings between day and night are credited for the dense, substantial leaf.

The tea comes in two shapes, flat like a Long Jing and curled. Flat tea is smooth and straight, emerald to yellow-green, and the cup is bright with a high aroma. Brew it like any sturdy green, and expect it to manage a few steeps.

Sub-regional names like Wenxian green tea and the Yangba teas of Kangxian sit inside this area, and each has its own followers. Longnan is the name to read as the broad label, with those as the more specific ones.
history:
Longnan Green Tea was registered as a protected agricultural geographical indication on 2 November 2016. In November 2019 it was listed among Gansu's Gan Wei farm product brands at the China International Agricultural Products Fair.

The appellation is new and the name itself is an administrative umbrella, so its history is largely that of the county teas within it. Little is documented about Longnan Green Tea as a single product before the registration.
